notes.heading: Compare rates and distributions before drawing a spatial conclusion
paragraphs: Fieldwork observations often differ in their duration, area or number of people exposed. Standardise those denominators before comparing totals. A mean can be affected strongly by a single extreme observation, so describe spread and inspect the raw values as well. Spatial sampling and time sampling answer different questions: distributing sites across neighbourhoods does not remove a morning-only bias. A defensible conclusion names the sampled places and times, notes the limits of the design and proposes a targeted improvement rather than merely asking for more data.

questions.prompt: Fictional pedestrian counts are 90 people in 15 minutes at A and 80 in 10 minutes at B. Compare rates and explain why the larger total is not the higher rate.
questions.answer: A averages 6 people per minute and B averages 8; B has the higher rate.
solution: Divide each count by its own observation duration.
Compare rates after standardising the unit.

questions.prompt: Fictional litter counts at five equal-area sites are 2,3,3,4,28. Find the mean and median, then explain what reporting only the mean could hide.
questions.answer: Mean 8 and median 3; the site with 28 strongly raises the mean and the sites are uneven.
solution: Sum to 40 and divide by 5; the middle ordered value is 3.
Report the outlier and range or raw values alongside the mean.
markingPoints: Explain the exceptional site and uneven distribution.

questions.prompt: A fictional study samples streets in every neighbourhood but counts traffic only from 08:00 to 08:15 on one weekday. What is improved by the spatial coverage, and what conclusion still cannot be supported?
questions.answer: It improves representation across sampled neighbourhoods. It does not establish typical daily or weekend traffic because time coverage is narrow.
solution: Separate the geographical sampling frame from the time frame.
Repeat at planned time periods and days before making a whole-week claim.
markingPoints: Propose sampling additional periods and days.
